summary: In Greek mythology and history, Phalanthus was the semi-legendary leader of the Spartan Partheniae and the founder of Tarentum (Taranto) in Magna Graecia. A Delphic oracle promised him success when he felt rain under a cloudless sky (aethra); the riddle was solved when his wife Aethra wept upon his head.
attribution: Adapted from Wikipedia, "Phalanthus (founder of Tarentum)" · CC BY-SA 4.0

sections.heading: Revolt in Sparta
paragraphs: The Partheniae — "sons of virgins," sons of unmarried Spartan women and perioeci — conspired with Phalanthus and the Epeunacti to revolt in the marketplace when Phalanthus, in full armor, pulled his helmet over his forehead. A tip to the ephors forestalled the rising: most wished to kill Phalanthus, but his lover Agathiadas warned that bloodshed would plunge Sparta into civil war. The herald instead proclaimed that Phalanthus should leave his helmet as it was; the Partheniae abandoned the plot and sought reconciliation. The attack was to have taken place during the Hyacinthia at Amyclae.

sections.heading: Founding Tarentum
paragraphs: Tarentum was a Lacedaemonian colony founded by Phalanthus. Setting out, he received a Delphic oracle that when he felt rain under a cloudless sky (aethra) he would conquer a territory and a city. Victories over the barbarians brought no city until, in despair, his wife Aethra — who had accompanied him — wept as she deloused his head; her tears wet him, and he understood the oracle. That night he took Tarentum, the largest and most prosperous city on the coast.

Tradition also held that before reaching Italy Phalanthus was shipwrecked in the Crissaean sea and brought ashore by a dolphin. Tarentine offerings at Delphi included statues of Taras and Phalanthus beside a dolphin, works associated with Onatas of Aegina and Ageladas of Argos.
